clue.text: Laughing at non-U African Queen?

indicators.note: non-U here tells the solver to drop the letter U from the word before it

parts.note: a Bantu is a member of a large group of African peoples
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone mocks the old film The African Queen, or a queen of Africa, as not upper-class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-U' is British slang for not upper-class; here it says to take U away from BANTU, leaving BANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Banter is teasing, good-humoured mockery, so it covers laughing at someone in a friendly way.

clue.text: Second and first positions of lever by friend of …

parts.note: B is the second letter, as in B for second class
I is the Roman numeral for one, so it stands for first
the settings of a gear lever are its gears

explanation.surface: Sounds like instructions for working a gear lever, trailing off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs on through the dots into 2-down: Big Ears is the friend of Noddy, Enid Blyton's little character. Big Ears also completes the proverb at 4-across.
explanation.definitionFit: In Enid Blyton's stories the bearded gnome with large ears is Noddy's closest companion, his best friend.

clue.text: … 24's 4 tern

definitions.meaning: 24 is Enid Blyton and 4 is LITTLE, so this means Enid Blyton's little wooden boy from Toyland
a kind of tropical tern, a seabird

explanation.walkthrough: The dots continue from 1-down, so the solver reads 'friend of Noddy' across the two clues.
explanation.definitionFit: Noddy is Blyton's small toy hero, and also the name of a dark tropical seabird of the tern family.

clue.text: Top man's agent in capital return

indicators.note: return asks for the whole assembled piece to be read backwards
in places the agent inside the capital city

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent

explanation.surface: A leading figure's representative is in the capital, on a return journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top man's' reads like a possessive, but the 's is a link word ('has'). 'return' turns the whole container backwards, not just the agent.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor rules an empire, the highest ruler of all, so he is the top man.

clue.text: Braveheart still 8's epic, hence "not in front of the children"

annotationWithheld.why: Braveheart still 8's epic, hence "not in front of the children" (6,8,4,3,4): the anagram gives the whole proverb LITTLE PITCHERS HAVE BIG EARS, but the group as held (4, 15, 12) leaves out 1-down BIG EARS, so the fodder has seven letters the filed answer cannot take
annotationWithheld.clue: Braveheart still 8's epic, hence "not in front of the children"

clue.text: Setter's set point — credit when object's discreditable

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself says I am, shortened to I'm
to set something down is to put it
E, for east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: The setter fixes a point at which praise must be given even for something shameful.
explanation.definitionFit: To impute is to attribute, usually blame or a fault, to someone, which is crediting them with something bad.

clue.text: Draw round nearly half the players for historic relay

indicators.note: round means the draw is wrapped around the other piece

parts.note: to draw an outline is to trace it

indicators.note: nearly half keeps just under half of the players' word, four of its nine letters

parts.note: an orchestra is a body of musical players

explanation.surface: A draw is made round some of the team for an old relay event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly half' keeps just under half of a nine-letter word: four letters, ORCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch race was an ancient Greek relay in which runners passed a lit torch, a historic contest.

clue.text: Genderless vegetable topped and tailed by sponsor of poetry

indicators.note: topped and tailed, as with beans, means the first and last letters of the run are removed

parts.note: neuter means having no gender
a pea is a vegetable

explanation.surface: A sexless vegetable trimmed at both ends by a patron of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: NEUTERPEA loses its first and last letters, N and A, leaving the Muse.
explanation.definitionFit: Euterpe is the Greek Muse of lyric poetry and music, so she inspires and patronises poets.

clue.text: Sorry range for one on blended tea

parts.note: a compass is the range or extent of something, as in the compass of a voice
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: blended says the letters of tea are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: An apology for a range of products, set on a tea blend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word; ATE is the anagram of TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling sorry for someone is feeling sympathy or pity, which is being compassionate.

clue.text: Old if unqualified

parts.note: the word that means elderly only when nothing follows it; given an age after it, as in 'twelve years', it means nothing of the kind

explanation.definitionFit: Aged on its own means elderly, while 'aged six' needs a number and says nothing about being old.

clue.text: Wealth is tedious if by it confined

indicators.note: confined means the second pair of pieces is shut inside the first

parts.note: prosy means dull and long-winded
per means by, as in per annum
taken as written

explanation.surface: Riches are boring if you are hemmed in by them.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosperity is the state of thriving financially, so it is a synonym for wealth.

clue.text: Bob or Tom spotted cockney solver

parts.note: spotted means saw
the solver is 'you', and a cockney would say your or you as yer

explanation.surface: Somebody called Bob or Tom catches sight of a London solver.
explanation.walkthrough: A cockney is a working-class Londoner, known for dropped sounds. Tom Sawyer is Mark Twain's hero; Bob Sawyer is a medical student in Dickens's Pickwick Papers.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs to two famous fictional characters: Twain's Tom and Dickens's Bob.

clue.text: See 4
Female instrumentalist and sailor among journalists

indicators.note: among puts the sailor inside the journalists

parts.note: the press is journalists as a body
an old salt is an experienced sailor

explanation.surface: A woman musician and a seaman find themselves among reporters.
explanation.definitionFit: A psaltress is a woman who plays the psaltery, an old stringed instrument.

clue.text: See 22
See 4
See 27
Feeding may be insincere

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters of feeding could become another word if rearranged

explanation.surface: Eating could be done without any real appetite.
explanation.definitionFit: Something feigned is pretended or put on, so it is insincere.

clue.text: Alien in tunnel is no intellectual

indicators.note: in puts the alien inside the tunnel

parts.note: the Simplon is a railway tunnel through the Alps between Switzerland and Italy
ET is the alien of the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: An extraterrestrial lost in a tunnel turns out not to be very bright.
explanation.definitionFit: A simpleton is a foolish, slow-witted person, the opposite of a thinker.

clue.text: One chasing order for fast food in Italy

indicators.note: chasing means the one comes after the other pieces

parts.note: PO stands for postal order
Lent is the Christian period of fasting
A means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: Someone pursues an order for a quick Italian meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word. 'fast food' looks like a single phrase, but 'fast' is LENT and 'food in Italy' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Polenta is an Italian dish of boiled cornmeal, a staple food of northern Italy.

clue.text: Gradual assimiliation means the world is not Conservative

indicators.note: not means the Conservative is removed from the word for the world

parts.note: the cosmos is the world or universe as an ordered whole

explanation.surface: Slow absorption means the world is no longer Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'means' is a link word. 'assimiliation' is printed this way, a slip for assimilation.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmosis is used figuratively for absorbing ideas or knowledge slowly and unconsciously.

clue.text: Man of faith replaces fascist's end with his head

indicators.note: replaces signals swapping the last letter of the fascist's name for another letter

parts.note: Sir Oswald Mosley led the British Union of Fascists in the 1930s

explanation.surface: A believer takes the place of a fascist's ending with his own head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end' names Y, the last letter of MOSLEY, and 'his head' is M, the first letter of the man of faith himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A Moslem, an older spelling of Muslim, is a follower of Islam, a man of faith.

clue.text: Business going bust should consolidate

parts.note: a firm is a business
a business going bust is down, as in gone under

explanation.surface: A company that collapses ought to merge its operations.
explanation.definitionFit: To firm down soil or a surface is to press it so it is compact, making it solid.

clue.text: Take another setter also to your heart?

definitions.text: Take another setter also to your heart?

parts.words: Take another setter also to your heart?
parts.note: the crossword setter asks to be loved, and a setter is also a breed of dog, so his pet must be cherished too

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb means that if you care for someone you must accept everything that comes with them.
explanation.definitionFit: The old saying asks that a loved one's companions, his pet included, be loved along with him.

clue.text: Opposed to a trick about a dog (wild) and a navigator

parts.note: V, for versus, means against or opposed to

indicators.note: about means the trick goes around the other piece

parts.note: a scam is a trick or swindle

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of a dog are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone against a dodge involving a wild dog, and a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' turns A DOG into ODAG. 'a navigator' looks like the whole definition, but its 'a' supplies the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: Vasco da Gama was the Portuguese explorer who first sailed from Europe to India round Africa.

clue.text: Old? Ninety? Born so as to make her a hundred and ten

definitions.text: Old? Ninety? Born so as to make her a hundred and ten

indicators.note: so as to make tells the solver to rework the earlier letters into a new name

explanation.surface: Asking whether she is old or ninety, and noting a birth date that makes her a hundred and ten.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of OLD NINETY and B gives the author, born in 1897, so a hundred and ten when the puzzle appeared in 2007.
explanation.definitionFit: The children's author was born in 1897, so she would have turned a hundred and ten that year.

clue.text: Top of sycamore tree in the window

indicators.note: top of picks out the first letter of sycamore

parts.note: the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: The highest part of a tree is visible through the window.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is the sliding frame holding the glass in a sash window, part of the window itself.

24's friends initially f-four with an animal around
